title: Nos Vemos en las Urnas · Development and execution plan
subtitle: 29 November 2026 election · English engineering plan · Spanish public product
summary: A free cited programme explorer and private progressive questionnaire, with a modern inclusive Spanish experience. Ten balanced starter questions lead to a neutral checkpoint and optional five-question blocks; checkpoints may show a permitted highest overlap without identifying a party; explicit finish reveals party identities, individual scores, explanations and citations. Reviewed evidence, English original code/docs, scoped regional/metric gates and no ML remain the baseline.

Feature implementation, methodology and all public release/collection approvals remain pending. Local scaffold evidence is not production certification.

sections.title: 1. Scope and user journey
sections.lead: Build both a programme explorer and a short policy questionnaire for the Congress election first. Both are free, with no account required.
items: Define “all” using the official confirmed candidacy register, rather than a hand-picked list of national parties. Until proclamation, label the registry provisional. Reconcile it after official publication and subsequent corrections or appeals.

Include parties, coalitions and elector groups by their actual ballot identity. Link shared programmes once and keep distinct local annexes. Do not merge coalition members’ positions unless the joint programme supports doing so.
Maintain a nationwide browse mode. Let users select a Congress constituency locally to see ballot availability; do not request an address, postcode, GPS location or voter identification.

Two equal entry points: (1) compare parties by topic with no questionnaire; (2) take the questionnaire and explore overlaps. Comparison includes proposals, conditions, quantified commitments where present, original citations and unknowns. Optional constituency selection and priorities remain local. Optional feedback is separately explained.

Deliver mobile web access, keyboard and screen-reader support, and Spanish as the default interface across public and editorial screens. Keep Catalan, Basque and Galician interfaces in scope; enable each only after its translations and political wording have been approved by fluent reviewers. Preserve exact original-language source quotations with separately labelled translations. All original application code and developer documentation use English.
MVP excludes tactical-voting advice, seat predictions, candidate personality rankings, historical-record fact checking, visitor accounts, political advertising, and social leaderboards.

Free means no payment for the questionnaire, comparisons, citations, results or ordinary exports. The project will publish its original application code and methodology under an open-source licence. Publish original editorial metadata and explanations under a suitable separate licence where rights permit; preserve rights and attribution for third-party programmes. Keep funding transparent; no political advertising or sale of political response data.

Congress-first matching is the current proposed release scope, shown clearly throughout the product. Archive relevant programme documents with their actual chamber and territorial scope. Keep any Senate availability and later matching separate; a Congress-only registry must not be advertised as covering all ballot options in both chambers.

Baseline access is public, free and without visitor accounts. “Private” means political answers and results remain local and metrics follow a separate approved flow; it does not mean the public evidence website has a private login. Editorial accounts are required and restricted. Invitation gating is outside the baseline scope.

Capability-based releases are explicit: registry/source explorer can publish first, the private questionnaire activates after its own evidence/method/privacy gates, reviewed regional locales activate for available surfaces, and metrics remain optional. Public badges describe what is actually enabled, not the eventual whole-project ambition.

The questionnaire stays party-neutral until the user explicitly finishes; the independent public programme explorer remains available without a quiz. After finish, provide scoped overlap insights and exact cited explanations for answered questions, plus further public policy information.

sections.title: 2. What “truth” means in the product
sections.lead: Separate source evidence, interpretation and real-world verification.
items: Source evidence: “The programme proposes X”, with an exact excerpt and locator. This is the primary product claim.
Interpretation: “This proposal supports the questionnaire statement.” Display the reasoning and the evidence status. A scoring judgement is an interpretation even when carefully reviewed.

Real-world verification: whether a promise is feasible, funded or delivered needs a separate evidence base. Do not present a manifesto quotation as proof that a factual claim is correct or that a promise will happen.

Use equal inclusion, wording, topic weighting, evidence rules and review standards for every candidacy. Equal standards do not require equal scores or inventing an opposing position when the evidence is absent.

Use neutral names and visual treatment, explain the method, disclose funding and editorial conflicts, and maintain a correction log. Parties may submit source corrections through the same process; they do not receive editorial vetoes.

Have two independent reviewers approve every scored position and question. Keep a named adjudication role for disagreement. Readers can challenge an excerpt or interpretation through a form that does not require revealing their quiz answers.

Separate source acquisition, position assessment, independent approval and release publication permissions. Record reviewer conflicts, independence and disputes. Two accounts owned by one person do not meet the review requirement. An adjudicator cannot silently waive evidence or quorum; unresolved mappings stay unscored.

sections.title: 3. Collect and version the programmes
sections.lead: The evidence workflow is likely to require more work than the questionnaire UI.
items: Create a source register per candidacy: official programme URL, election, geographical scope, language, publication date if known, retrieval timestamp, version and availability status. Distinguish “not found”, “not yet published”, “published but unreviewed” and “reviewed”. Do not imply every candidacy will publish a programme.

Prefer official party or coalition websites and verified programme documents. A 2023 programme, news article or campaign interview is not a substitute for a 2026 programme. Keep supplementary commitments and historical material separately labelled and outside the default score.

Save an immutable original and SHA-256 hash, subject to publication and reuse rights. Extract text with OCR where needed. Retain PDF page index, printed page label, section, paragraph and optional bounding box. For HTML, preserve a timestamped snapshot and stable text locator.
Each scored position must carry a short exact quotation, surrounding context, original language, separately labelled translation if used, original URL, page/section, document hash and review record.

AI may propose passages, translations, summaries and question mappings from public documents. Human reviewers approve them against the original. Never send user answers or inferred matches to an AI provider.

Detect changes against the source register during development and operations. Re-review changed passages; publish a new version of the dataset and mappings. Preserve old releases so a result can be reproduced with its original version.

Do not claim complete programme coverage until the registry has been reconciled and every candidacy has an explicit source status. A missing programme stays visible in browsing and is marked as insufficient evidence for scoring.

Availability assessment as of 7 October: spot checks established access to historical PSOE and PP programme PDFs and a Sumar 23J programme page. They did not establish a complete set of official programmes for November 2026. The election was called only recently; keep 2023 material clearly historical and outside the current-election score.

Define reusable programme scopes before expanding the matrix: one national programme may support many ballot candidacies, while territorial annexes or joint coalition texts require their own applicability records. Reuse approved evidence only where the exact document, question and scope are identical; never inherit a member party’s stance into a coalition without joint-source support.

A release validator checks source authenticity, election, chamber and territorial applicability, quotation accuracy, context, locator resolution, document hash, rights status and independent approvals. Hashes detect changed bytes; they do not establish that a document is authentic or legally redistributable.

Fetch only approved public sources. Bound size, redirects, elapsed time and retries; protect against private-network/metadata URLs and DNS rebinding. Parse/OCR PDFs and snapshots in an isolated process with resource limits. Treat extracted HTML, embedded links and AI-facing document instructions as untrusted content.

Record last successful source check, last document change and last review separately. Broken or changed external links do not silently invalidate an already archived reviewed quotation; mark access status, verify authenticity and revise the release when interpretation changes.

A not-stated position means no explicit position was found under the documented review of the applicable programme. Record review/search extent and OCR limitations; do not claim exhaustive absence from a quick search. A missing or unreviewed programme is a source-availability status, not a reviewed assertion that the party has no policy.

sections.title: 4. Progressive questions without forced choices
sections.lead: Ten accessible balanced starter questions, followed by optional five-question blocks from a larger reviewed bank.
items: A: strongly agree. B: somewhat agree. C: somewhat disagree. D: strongly disagree. Add separate “neither agree nor disagree”, “I am unsure” and “skip” choices. Neutral is a real answer; uncertainty and skipping are not scored.

Propose a reviewed bank of 60–100 distinct policy questions, subject to actual evidence and review capacity, across 8–10 domains: housing, taxation and public spending, work and pensions, health and care, education, energy and climate, migration, territorial governance, rights and institutions, and EU/foreign policy. These are an initial editorial proposal, not a validated question bank.

Choose specific policy distinctions supported by the collected corpus. Avoid slogans, assumptions of bad intent, leading preambles, two policies in one question, and choices that bundle unrelated beliefs.

Keep ABCD as answer labels, not ideological categories. Do not presume A is left-wing or D is right-wing. If a question asks people to choose between different policies, use a separately published compatibility rubric rather than pretending the letters form an ordered scale.

Design examples only: “El Estado debería limitar las subidas del alquiler en las zonas declaradas tensionadas.” “España debería fijar una fecha de cierre para las centrales nucleares existentes.” “Deberían ampliarse las vías legales de entrada para trabajar en España.” No party position is asserted for these examples; remove or revise them unless the 2026 corpus supports useful, fair comparisons.

Ask importance by domain, optionally, using simple levels such as normal, important and very important. Publish equal-domain defaults. Let users change priorities locally; avoid repeatedly counting essentially the same policy.

Pilot for comprehension, completion burden, question-order effects, translation consistency, perceived neutrality and how scores change when a question is removed. Review sensitive or misunderstood wording before release.

Before freezing questions, publish the topic budget and selection criteria; measure overlap and missingness across programme scopes. Pilot blinded independent coding, conditions/negation, duplicate issue coverage, partly answered topics and regional translations. Use synthetic response profiles for scoring sensitivity. Do not retain participants’ real answer vectors, ideology labels or voting intentions to conduct the pilot.

The first checkpoint is after ten presented questions, with actual numeric-answer count separate from skipped/unsure responses. It shows progress, optional policy-permitted highest overlap without identifying a party, and stop/+5 choices; no party-specific score mapping. Only an explicit finish reveals cited results; users can also leave without revealing.
Adaptive ordering selects useful reviewed distinctions and fills topic gaps locally. It never guesses unanswered beliefs, chooses a target party or uses acceptance metrics as its objective.
The bank size is an editorial capacity proposal, not a quota. Every scored mapping still requires exact current-election evidence and two genuinely independent approvals.

sections.title: 5. Transparent matching and overlaps
sections.lead: Use an inspectable five-point policy-distance calculation, with known-evidence overlap, weighted coverage and explicitly shared comparison sets.
items: Detailed method version: policy-distance-v1.0.0. User answers use −2, −1, 0, +1, +2; unsure and skip have no numeric value. Party positions use a published commitment/support rubric rather than inferred emotional intensity. Only reviewed current-election programme positions are scored.

Normalize question base weights within each answered topic and normalize the user’s topic priorities across answered topics. Keep those original weights fixed when assessing each party’s evidence coverage. Topics have equal default influence regardless of question count.

Per-question similarity is 1 − |user code − party code| / 4. For known positions, K is the sum of weight × similarity and C is the known weight. Report 100 × K/C as an index out of 100, alongside 100 × C evidence coverage. An index is not the probability of affiliation or the literal proportion of manifesto promises accepted.

For missing party positions, the smallest possible similarity is 1 − max(|user code + 2|, |user code − 2|)/4; the largest is 1. Add those weighted possible contributions to K to form a full-question lower/upper bound. These are coding-based missing-evidence bounds, not statistical confidence intervals. With C = 0, show an unavailable score.

Direct comparisons use the exact same answered questions with reviewed positions for every member of the explicit comparison cohort. Use the same original weights, renormalized by their common total. Do not silently exclude candidates with poor documentation or combine comparisons using different question sets into one ordering.

Initial pilot thresholds for a roughly 30-question release: 20 scored user answers over 6 topics, 15 common questions over 6 topics, and 80% common weighted coverage. A proposed 3-point grouping convention avoids overstating near scores. These settings must be reviewed, piloted, published and versioned; they are not validated scientific thresholds.

A pure browser-compatible reference engine and clearly fictional arithmetic fixtures now implement this proposal. Fifteen meaningful verification groups pass. Real programmes, question selection, party codings, privacy integration and the production Laravel app remain unvalidated development work.

The all-candidacy shared intersection may be empty or too narrow even when many programmes are available. Treat this as an evidence limitation, not an engineering defect. Keep every candidacy visible, show documented overlaps and missing evidence, and permit explicitly selected comparisons only under the published policy. Do not promise a universal best-party result.

Partly answered topics retain their chosen topic priority distributed among answered questions. Explain this behaviour and show response coverage per topic. Pilot sensitivity to skipped answers, one answered question in a high-priority topic, leave-one-question-out changes and alternate ordinal coding; publish material fragility without calling it a statistical confidence interval.

Before release, check finite bounded numeric weights, finite normalized totals, similarity/index bounds, unique IDs, approval metadata, schema compatibility and the comparison cohort. Detect arithmetic/schema failures before publication and withhold personal scores on an incompatible or corrupt bundle.

The adaptive flow is specified separately as adaptive-questionnaire-v0.2.0-proposed. Ten-question output is provisional; existing 20-answer/15-common-question reference thresholds stay explicit until a separately validated short-mode policy is approved.

Preferred adaptive weighting fixes topic/family/question budgets across the entire pinned bank. This is a proposed method change requiring a new reviewed algorithm version; the v1 reference and its 15 checks remain unchanged.
Response coverage, manifesto evidence coverage and deterministic result stability are separate. Never present an invented confidence percentage or a probability that a person belongs to a party.

Stopping bounds must use the same scoring target/weights as the published adaptive method. The fixed-bank diagnostic cannot certify v1's changing answered-only weighting. Identical parties, missing programme evidence or skipped answers can prevent a stronger conclusion.

Overlap strength is the main permitted result after explicit finish; coverage/stability are supporting information. Indices are independent rather than shares summing to 100%, can rise or fall with new answers, and never identify a person's party or prescribe a vote. Insufficient common evidence suppresses a broad highest-match headline.

sections.title: 6. Privacy architecture
sections.lead: Private is a set of testable data-flow rules, not an assurance that no technical trace can ever exist.
items: Questionnaire answers, importance settings, constituency and results stay in browser memory by default. Private reflection is also local unless the person separately opts into an approved anonymous metrics flow. Clear resets the session; reload starts again. Saving to the device or exporting requires an explicit action and explains shared-device risk.

Serve the same complete reviewed election bundle to every user, independent of their answers or selected constituency. Run deterministic scoring in the browser. Source links are user-initiated. Offer an offline bundle for users who need to avoid hosting access traces.

Core servers store public-source documents, editorial records and released data, with no questionnaire response database. Any approved metrics pipeline is separately operated and outputs aggregates into a restricted dashboard. It may need short-lived encrypted protocol records while aggregating, followed by deletion; do not describe that as zero processing. Editorial admin access is separate and restricted. Invitation identity must never be linked to quiz responses.

Self-host fonts and assets. Exclude advertising, tracking pixels, third-party analytics, session replay, remote questionnaire APIs and behavioural recommendation systems. Keep answers out of URLs, referrers, crash reports, breadcrumbs and logs.

Document hosting, CDN and security-log behaviour. Disable unnecessary logs and identifiers, restrict unavoidable security data, minimize retention and verify providers’ configuration. The host necessarily handles connection metadata while online; do not promise absolute anonymity.

Use transport security, restrictive browser content policy, dependency review, safe rendering of extracted text, sanitised document handling and audited administrative access. Treat fetched programmes as untrusted input to both extraction and AI workflows.

Political opinions are specially protected under GDPR Article 9. Spain’s LOPDGDD Article 9 adds restrictions on consent for identifying ideology. Obtain specialist review of the actual data flows, lawful bases and DPIA requirements before launch; client-side processing reduces exposure but does not automatically resolve every legal question.

Publish an accurate privacy notice and data-flow inventory. Public editorial methodology may coexist with private user responses. Metrics participation is optional and declining it preserves the full free service. The plan and any prototype remain local unless separately authorised for deployment.

Privacy claims apply precisely to local political inputs. Public page/source navigation can reveal ordinary browsing metadata to hosting or external party sites. Disclose this distinction, suppress referrers and avoid automatic remote document embeds. Show the archived accessible excerpt locally; external originals open only after an intentional click.

Inventory non-quiz personal data separately: editorial accounts and reviewer records, optional correction contact details and necessary restricted security logs. Give each a purpose, access policy, retention rule and deletion process. Public professional reviewer attribution is a separate governance choice, not a reason to link quiz responses.

Inspect browser autofill, back/forward cache, reload, language switching, clear/reset, downloads and accidental crash paths. No answer persistence by default. Keep caches/service workers limited to public assets if introduced; offline packages contain public code/data only unless a user deliberately exports personal results.

Declare political inputs as sensitive in engineering reviews. Prohibit automatic error-report payloads, analytics breadcrumbs and support attachments containing answers or affinities. Public issue templates ask for synthetic reproduction steps, never a person’s political profile.

Public application routes must not serialize political state into query strings, form submissions or full-request logs. Use browser event handling that prevents accidental form/Enter submissions and verify that actual hosting/error middleware does not capture sensitive payloads. Test keyboard and unexpected-error paths, not only deliberate clicks.

sections.title: 7. Useful metrics that respect the promise
sections.lead: Include useful anonymous metrics as a planned feature. Keep collection disabled until the actual anonymity and legal design have been verified.
items: Three metric groups: editorial completeness and quality; coarse service usage; optional post-result feedback. Editorial metrics use public documents and review records and require no personal response collection.

Editorial metrics: source-status coverage by candidacy, reviewed question-position coverage, broken source links, review disagreements, update age and correction turnaround. Calculate these from each dataset release.

Optional usage counters: questionnaire starts and completions, comparison visits, citation opens and generic failures. Send no party, question ID, selected topic, constituency, answer vector, result, browser fingerprint, account or persistent visitor ID. Explain collection before participation. Ratios based on these counters describe events, not reliably unique people.

Optional post-result questions: “Was the comparison clear?”; “Does it reflect your policy preferences?”; “Would you consider voting differently after reviewing this?” Include unsure and prefer-not-to-answer options. For willingness to reconsider, ask no intended party or matched party. Participants can submit one feedback item or skip all of them.

Proposed measures: clarity share and perceived-accuracy share among submitted feedback responses, with separate unsure counts; willingness-to-reconsider share among that question’s responding submissions; and the approximate completion-event ratio. Specify numerator, denominator, consent scope, release version and time period. Do not label these figures as national opinion, unique voters, causal effects or verified changes in votes.

Start with coarse global totals or non-overlapping weekly batches, not demographic, regional or per-party breakdowns. Keep the dashboard private by default. Suppress small cells, restrict repeated overlapping queries, document sampling and duplicate-submission limitations, and apply an assessed differential-privacy policy where appropriate. A sample-size threshold alone does not establish anonymity.

For sensitive feedback, evaluate a maintained secure-aggregation implementation with two independently controlled aggregators and a collector that receives only approved batch totals. The IETF DAP design is a relevant work-in-progress reference. Under its honest-aggregator assumption, no aggregator sees an individual measurement in the clear. Infrastructure operators must not be able to collude through shared administrative access.

Secure aggregation protects measurement values; it does not by itself hide source IPs, timing or contribution patterns. Assess an independent relay, log configuration, task metadata, batch-selection attacks, aggregate differencing, retention and shared-operator risks. Use an established implementation and specialist review; do not invent cryptography.

Permit only a fixed metric schema. Delete encrypted per-report state after a documented batch lifecycle; discard undersized batches at their expiry rather than retaining them indefinitely. Keep no recoverable questionnaire responses. Final retention periods and batch sizes must follow the threat model and operational tests.

Opt-in is a product choice, not proof of a lawful basis or true anonymity. Obtain the applicable privacy and legal assessment before collection. If the metrics design is not ready, launch the free questionnaire and comparison with editorial metrics and local feedback; add collection once verified.

Do not optimize wording for flattering matches or changed votes. No political targeting, per-party persuasion dashboard, sale of profiles, or training on user responses. If electoral survey findings are ever published, assess LOREG Article 69 restrictions separately.

All non-editorial measurement is disabled by default in the baseline deployment. Optional usage and post-result feedback activate only after the fixed schema, transport, operators, consent, legal basis, retention and aggregation-release rules pass their separate gate. The core launches without them if necessary.

Do not resolve anonymous-count abuse by quietly introducing IP hashes, fingerprinting or persistent identifiers. Label event/submission denominators honestly and document bot/repeat-submission uncertainty. Choose abuse controls only after assessing their privacy tradeoffs; publish no population or unique-voter estimates from self-selected feedback.

Private dashboard access does not establish anonymous collection. Public aggregate publication is outside baseline scope; any later publication requires an additional legal and statistical review, including electoral-survey rules. No per-party or per-constituency persuasion statistics.

sections.title: 8. Engineering structure and backlog
sections.lead: Use Laravel conventions for the application and editorial workflow, with Boost assisting development and a small browser module performing private matching.
items: Planned stack: Laravel, PostgreSQL, Blade for programme browsing and comparisons, and a small JavaScript/TypeScript questionnaire module using the released evidence bundle. Use a database-backed queue and scheduler for public-document jobs and release generation. Cache public pages and assets as traffic requires. Boost is a development dependency; Rubix ML is outside the first release.

Core records: Election; Candidacy with chamber and constituency availability; ProgrammeDocument with source, scope, language and hash; EvidenceExcerpt with page, context and translation; Question with domain and answer scale; PositionAssessment with question, candidacy, value/status and evidence; ReviewDecision; DatasetRelease with rubric and algorithm versions.

Candidacy scope comes from official election data. Every assessment references evidence and every release pins document versions. Local results pin the questionnaire, dataset, weights and algorithm versions so calculations can be reproduced.
Backlog A — governance and registry: editorial charter, inclusion rules, scope, source statuses, privacy inventory and legal design review.
Backlog B — corpus: acquisition, archive, extraction/OCR, passage locators, source diffs, review queue and publication checks.
Backlog C — questionnaire: topic matrix, wording, reviewed evidence mapping, original-language support, importance controls and pilot.
Backlog D — results: local scorer, coverage and interval calculations, topic explanations, shared-basis comparisons, source viewer and reset/export.
Backlog E — release: privacy/network verification, accessibility checks, neutral presentation review, corrections process, release manifests and operations runbook.

Backlog F — anonymous measurement: metric definitions, a fixed schema, consent UI, established secure aggregation, independent operator arrangement, batch-release policy, privacy review, load tests and a restricted aggregate dashboard. This work must not become a dependency of basic questionnaire or comparison availability.

Use standard Laravel routes, controllers, validation, policies, models, migrations, jobs and tests. Keep scoring rules in a small inspectable browser module, with synthetic fixtures documenting expected outputs. Public APIs serve reviewed evidence and citations, never accept questionnaire answer vectors.

Boost provides Laravel-focused guidelines, skills, documentation lookup and application-inspection MCP tools. Restrict it to local development with public or synthetic data; do not give coding agents production databases, credentials or private metrics access. Its value is a consistent development workflow, not a trained electoral model.

Backlog G — language policy: English identifiers and semantic translation keys; Spanish baseline catalogs in lang/es plus reviewed ca/gl/eu catalogs; Spanish default/fallback; a localized matching presentation adapter; public question/content translations; static checks, browser checks and fluent copy review. Keep the model/table pluralizer in English. Read project-wide AGENTS.md and .cursor/rules/project-language.mdc before implementation.

Maintain a modular Laravel application rather than separate services for every feature: registry/evidence, editorial review, release publication and public browsing. Local scoring is a separate pure browser module. Only the optional aggregation protocol may require independent infrastructure. No production service, hosting purchase or public deployment is performed by this planning work.
Actual local foundation: Laravel v13.35.0, Boost v2.10.2, Blade, Vite 8 and Tailwind 4. SQLite is local only. No Rubix, visitor authentication or questionnaire submission endpoint is installed.

Backlog H — modern inclusive experience: review civic identity and responsive Spanish journey states, implement accessible shared components and restrained motion, then verify comprehension across ages/abilities and calibrated real-device speed/recovery. All UI surfaces follow experienceDesign and section 28.

sections.title: 9. Proposed delivery calendar
sections.lead: Dates are proposed checkpoints, not a launch promise. Target a reviewed core release by 16 November; preserve the 29 November election deadline and the 13–27 November campaign window.
rows: Registry model, privacy design, rubric and provisional source inventory
Acquisition/archive pipeline, source viewer and local scoring skeleton
Draft question matrix, independent mappings and source-backed explanations
Reconcile official candidacies as published; review coverage, comprehension and gaps
Network/privacy checks, scoring verification, accessibility and neutrality review
Resolve findings, publish methodology and freeze the reviewed release
Launch the approved scope; keep visible source-status gaps and support corrections
Review new programme versions, patch defects and preserve released datasets
items: Staffing is unassigned. The earlier two-engineer assumption is a provisional starting point, not a validated estimate; independent editorial capacity is the limiting dependency. Measure review/extraction/translation effort in a pilot before committing to the nationwide scoring matrix.

Pilot the workflow on a disclosed subset to estimate review effort, then expand to every confirmed candidacy. Do not present a subset as the final all-party service. If programmes are late or evidence is insufficient, launch the cited explorer while holding back an overall ranking.

Election and campaign dates are verified in the decree. Development dates and roles are recommendations. Reconcile candidacies against actual official publications rather than treating a calculated date as proof that the final list exists.

By the proposed 14 October checkpoint, name the operator, engineering/release owner, editorial lead, independent reviewers, adjudicator and fluent-language reviewers; record their available hours, funding and conflicts. These are required decisions with no assigned people yet.

By the proposed 20 October checkpoint, measure pilot throughput and a full-matrix coverage forecast. If capacity is insufficient, prioritize the complete registry, cited source explorer and reviewed comparisons; hold overall ranking instead of reducing review standards.
Regional interface activation and anonymous metrics are gated additions. They never block a complete Spanish core, and they have no promised launch date until their own acceptance evidence exists.

At beta and after each programme change, re-check evidence coverage, source authenticity, release integrity and operational ownership. Dates never override a failed gate. A cited explorer may launch while scoring remains unavailable.
Dates are planning targets. Use the dependency graph and applicable approval gates below; source publication, reviewer capacity and failed checks override any calendar target.

sections.title: 10. Release gates and meaningful verification
sections.lead: Publish only the behaviour that the evidence and privacy checks support.
items: Completeness: every confirmed candidacy is represented with ballot availability and a source status. Every scored question-position cell has an approved excerpt and review history. No unpublished or historical programme is silently substituted.

Evidence: two reviewers can reproduce the interpretation from the original document; conditional wording is retained; page links resolve; OCR and translations have been checked. The dataset, rubric and corrections log are versioned.

Scoring: test missing, ambiguous and conflicting evidence; neutral versus skipped answers; domain weighting; near ties; and reproducibility. Identical positions must yield identical scores. Reordering parties must not change results. Unknown positions must never become opposition or neutrality.

Coverage: check interval bounds against complete synthetic cases and extremes; verify common-question comparisons use the same weights and evidence set; suppress overall ranking when evidence is inadequate.

Privacy: inspect network traffic while answering, changing weights, viewing results, resetting and exporting. Questionnaire answers, matches and constituency choices must stay local. Optional reflection contributions may leave only through the separately explained, consented and verified aggregation flow. Test consent refusal, error paths and logs against these rules.

Usability and neutrality: test mobile and keyboard flows, screen-reader labels, clarity of unknown evidence, citation comprehension and a pilot spanning differing political preferences without retaining ideology profiles.

Governance: publish ownership and funding, settle reviewer disputes, complete the relevant privacy/legal review, and assign an owner and turnaround target for corrections. Maintain a way to withdraw a disputed mapping promptly.

Metrics release gate: verify the real collection flow, transport metadata, operator separation, minimum batch and expiry behaviour, deletion, privacy-budget/query limits, denominators, consent and legal assessment. Do not advertise anonymity solely because a vendor or library uses that label.

Open-source verification: release the scoring code, method and reviewed evidence bundle; link the deployed code commit and data release; provide repeatable build instructions and artifact hashes; independently verify the served browser assets where possible. A server-displayed version string alone does not prove the production deployment.

Language release gate: Spanish is complete across public/editorial screens, accessibility attributes, errors, downloads and user-facing documentation. Every enabled regional locale must also have complete, fluent-reviewed interface and question translations. CI checks locale key coverage, interpolation/plural forms, prohibited hardcoded UI strings and unresolved keys; browser checks cover normal, empty and failure paths. Review original code identifiers, comments, schemas and developer documentation for English. Verify switching locale preserves scores and citations.

Decision status: public free access, Spanish default, reviewed regional interfaces, English code and local deterministic matching are baseline choices. Operator identity, staffing, licences, budget/providers, final comparison thresholds and optional aggregation operators remain unresolved. Resolve each required decision before its dependent task; do not label planning decisions as completed implementation.

Readiness is evidence-driven. Requirements REQ-01 through REQ-18, tasks TASK-01 through TASK-15, risks and decisions below define verification and fallback behaviour. Owner labels are proposed roles; actual accountable people must be named before beta or deployment.
The explicit, strict GATE-00–GATE-08 records below control execution. Earlier checklist gates remain acceptance criteria, not independent permission to deploy.

Experience release acceptance includes UX-01–UX-06: actual WCAG 2.2 AA scope, additional reduced-motion/large-control targets, meaningful mixed-age/assistive-technology comprehension and shipped-device performance/recovery. Planning prose and automated scores cannot pass it.

sections.title: 11. Existing competition and positioning
sections.lead: There are close alternatives already. This is a primary-site spot check on 7 October 2026, not a full security or editorial audit.
rows: Programme questions, topic comparisons, party browsing and affinity test
Very close product scope. Its current methodology reports positions pending literal citations and review. Current-election programmes are labelled pending.
56-question test, 10 parties, topic browsing and aggregate barometer
Its privacy policy describes storing test responses and an IP-derived HMAC. That is a different collection design from device-only matching.
Short election-specific tests and topic match results
Publishes a deterministic distance formula; methodology uses programmes, statements and parliamentary material. Its financing page mentions optional premium reports.
Historical reference for the comparison experience; do not treat the 2023 comparator as a reviewed November 2026 dataset.
items: A questionnaire plus comparison is already an existing category. Our proposed position is narrower and testable: current-election-only scoring, literal page-level quotations for every scored cell, independent review, equal inclusion, visible unknowns, free access and local response processing.

These observations come from the sites’ own published descriptions. They do not certify their neutrality, source accuracy, actual network behaviour or legal compliance. Competitors may improve their datasets before launch; avoid claims of being the first, only or inherently most neutral tool.

The core evidence dataset can become the project’s strongest contribution: a reviewed catalogue that supports both interfaces and can be inspected independently. Consider appropriate reuse or collaboration if compatible data and licences exist; no outreach is authorised by this plan.

sections.title: 12. Can we obtain the relevant information?
sections.lead: Likely most published programme material, but completeness of parties and completeness of policy answers are different goals.
items: The realistic commitment is a complete official candidacy registry plus an explicit source status for each entry. No application can obtain a programme that has not been published, or turn vague text into a precise commitment without interpretation.

Historical spot checks found the PSOE 2023 PDF at 272 pages, the PP 23J PDF at 112 pages, and an official Sumar programme page. This supports testing extraction and citation workflows now. These sources are historical; they do not establish 2026 policy positions.

There is no verified complete set of November 2026 programmes in this assessment. Search absence alone is not proof of non-publication. Maintain an official-domain source register and repeat checks as documents become available.

Expected gaps: late releases, scanned files, regional annexes, coalition changes, multiple language versions, broken links, vague promises and topics not addressed. Record conditions and scope rather than forcing a stance.

Use the same taxonomy in both interfaces. A comparison entry should retain actor, action, beneficiary, amount or deadline when specified, conditions, territorial scope and source passage. Separate editor summaries from exact original text.

Recommended next development milestone: a source-status inventory for all confirmed or provisionally announced candidacies, plus an extraction/review pilot across national, regional and coalition documents. Measure reviewer effort before committing to a comprehensive question matrix.

items: The Laravel choice changes the earlier static-only hosting assumption: budget for a PHP runtime, PostgreSQL, a queue worker and a scheduler. A single modest host can run those processes initially; benchmark before choosing its size or buying a plan. Provider selection and price remain open.

A static CDN is still useful for browser assets and reviewed release bundles. Cloudflare documents free static-asset requests, but that service does not directly run this Laravel PHP application. Do not present its free static tier or US$5 Worker minimum as a Laravel hosting quote.

R2 Standard remains a possible source archive: its limited free tier includes 10 GB-month storage, 1 million Class A operations and 10 million Class B operations per month, with free internet egress. Operation overages can incur charges; verify limits, location and logging against the actual requirements.

Free for users is a product commitment. Hosting, domains, backups, editorial review and independent metrics operations require an operating budget or contributed resources. Publish funding and costs without disclosing credentials or private operational data.

Laravel jobs may call an isolated extraction/OCR tool when ordinary PHP extraction is insufficient. Boost assists application development; neither tool makes source interpretation or user matching dependent on ML.

Do not send questionnaire answers to Laravel, a remote score endpoint or an AI provider. Public hosting handles connection metadata; configure and document logs, providers and retention independently of publishing the source code.
Avoid a GPU server, Kubernetes cluster, model endpoint or vector database for the first release. Add capacity only after measuring document-processing workload and realistic campaign traffic.

Keep public data cacheable and use graceful degradation. Collector failure or optional analytics budget exhaustion must leave programme comparisons and local questionnaire results usable. Document backups, restore steps and quota behaviour.

Choose a funded operational budget before selecting providers: PHP/DB hosting, archive/egress/requests, backups, domain, OCR or optional public-content AI, reviewer/translation effort and a contingency. Free access does not imply zero operating cost. No costs or provider purchases have been committed.

Publish immutable cacheable release assets. Once loaded, local scoring works without Laravel. Plan a static release index/source explorer and downloadable offline package for backend outages; verify them before advertising outage resilience. Never silently substitute stale or mixed data.

Proposed engineering targets to calibrate in the pilot: compressed core public bundle at most 5 MiB; local scoring p95 at most 100 ms on an agreed entry-level reference device; warm public-page p95 at most 1.5 s with under 1% errors during a 30-minute test at three times the agreed peak. Measure actual corpus/traffic before finalizing these budgets.

Proposed recovery targets: daily encrypted off-host editorial/source backups, maximum 24-hour recovery point and four-hour recovery time. A successful restore drill with released hashes and review permissions must demonstrate feasibility. Metrics records, if later introduced, follow their own short lifecycle and must not be copied into long-lived editorial backups.

Proposed inclusive experience budgets separately constrain initial UI to 300 KiB, validated cold questionnaire readiness to 5 s on the agreed named device/network, and local selector/bounds to 100 ms p95. LCP/INP/CLS lab targets follow official good thresholds, with controlled evidence explicitly labelled. The 5 MiB public-bundle ceiling never excuses slow startup; no default RUM/quiz telemetry is introduced.

sections.title: 14. Do we need machine learning?
sections.lead: No custom trained model or model-serving infrastructure is needed for matching or comparison.
items: The matching algorithm is a published distance calculation over user answers, domain weights and reviewed party positions. It is deterministic and can be tested with synthetic cases. It does not learn a person’s ideology from other users.

The comparison tool reads structured, reviewed proposals and citations. Ordinary topic filtering and browser text search are enough for the first release; embeddings and a vector database are optional later conveniences.

Useful optional AI assistance happens in the editorial pipeline: suggesting relevant passages, draft summaries, proposed question mappings, translation drafts and source changes. Require original-document verification before anything is published. Conventional OCR may itself use ML, but that does not require training our own political classifier.

Never score from an unreviewed generated summary or auto-fill a missing party position. Do not send user responses to model providers, fine-tune on them, or train models to maximize result acceptance or willingness to switch votes.

A natural-language chatbot would add inference cost, citation-validation work and opportunities for unsupported claims. It is outside the first release. We can keep the core useful and free through reviewed search, comparisons and local scoring.

Most critical work is editorial: defensible question choice, accurate evidence mapping, treatment of missing information and independent review. More sophisticated ML does not solve those judgement and governance requirements.
Laravel Boost is AI tooling for development, installed as a development dependency. It does not require adding Rubix ML, an electoral training dataset or a user-facing prediction model.

sections.title: 15. Open-source verification and community trust
sections.lead: Open source lets people inspect and reproduce behaviour. It cannot prove personal intentions, neutral editorial judgement or private server practices by itself.
items: Publish the original Laravel code, browser scoring module, data schemas, question-selection method, weighting and missing-evidence rules. Publish synthetic scoring fixtures and meaningful invariance tests so reviewers can reproduce results without using real people’s answers.

Publish the reviewed public-evidence dataset with exact source references, programme versions, position interpretations, uncertainty states and correction history. If an original programme cannot be redistributed, provide its official link, hash and locators with quotations permitted by applicable rights. Do not relicense third-party text as project-owned material.

Tie every deployed release to a source commit, dependency lockfiles, algorithm version and evidence-bundle hash. Supply repeatable build and self-hosting instructions. Aim for reproducible browser assets and provide an independent verification procedure; hashes and a self-reported commit alone do not certify private backend behaviour.

Provide a clearly labelled source/release link in the product and an offline or local mode. People should be able to inspect the scoring implementation and run the questionnaire without submitting responses to the operator.

Show the same reviewed dataset and scoring code to all users. Preserve source and data release history. Announce changes to wording, weights or party mappings with their reasons so later reviewers can assess whether edits favour a party.

Publish editorial criteria, funding, ownership, reviewer conflicts and how disputed mappings are resolved. Require independent evidence review and use the same correction process for every party. Contributions are welcome; source-backed review remains necessary before merging political interpretations.

Use public issue and pull-request workflows for ordinary evidence corrections and code changes, plus a private security-reporting channel. Make it clear that contributors must not attach their political questionnaire responses, personal information or secrets to public issues.

Open-source the optional metrics protocol, fixed schema, consent flow and aggregate-release policy. Keep individual inputs, production credentials, encrypted report state and private operational records out of the repository. Source publication does not replace the anonymity assessment.

Recommended code licence for consideration: AGPL-3.0-only, if preserving source availability for modified network-served versions is a priority. Section 13 requires a modified version to offer Corresponding Source to its remote users. MIT is a simpler permissive alternative with no comparable network-source requirement. Final licence choice is still open; neither licence guarantees zero-price hosting or neutral behaviour.

Use a separate licensing decision for original editorial data and documentation. Record provenance and third-party rights. Before public release, confirm contributor rights, the licence text, dependency compatibility and that the repository contains no secrets or user data.

sections.title: 16. Detailed algorithm and worked arithmetic
sections.lead: All rows below are generated from fictional parties and synthetic answers. They assert nothing about real Spanish parties or users.
items: The complete specification covers evidence schemas, stance coding, topic weights, distance calculation, source coverage, missing-position bounds, shared comparisons, explanation generation, privacy boundaries and meaningful checks.
Party Z’s apparent 100/100 uses just one known position and 25% weighted coverage. The full three-party ordering is withheld because shared evidence is inadequate.

An explicit X-versus-Y comparison uses five common questions carrying 83.3% of the answer weight. On that identical set, X scores 90/100 and Y 80/100. Individual indices on different known question sets must not be sorted as if they were the same measure.

The toy example uses smaller, explicitly labelled comparison thresholds appropriate to its six questions and three topics. The proposed broad real-release thresholds would withhold an overall ordering for such a short questionnaire.

The local outputs directory contains matching-algorithm-specification.html, matching-engine.mjs, matching-example.json and matching-example-results.json. They are proposal/reference materials, not a published service.

The new adaptive specification is a planning supplement. It proposes whole-bank fixed weights, unasked-answer bounds and a deterministic next-question selector; it does not modify or certify the existing v1 reference.

sections.title: 17. Spanish default, regional interfaces, English code
sections.lead: Project-wide requirement: Spanish is the complete default interface; Catalan, Basque and Galician interfaces remain in scope with fluent review before activation. All original code and developer documentation are English. Translations and source evidence are content data.
items: Spanish is the default for every public and editorial/admin screen: navigation, forms, questions, answer labels, result explanations, citations, errors, empty states, consent/privacy pages, help, accessibility labels, metadata, charts, exports and user-facing notifications. Enabled regional interfaces cover the same product surfaces. Developer planning documents and repository contributor docs remain English.

English applies to original variables, functions, classes, types, namespaces, files/directories, route names and slugs, commands, database tables/columns, enum/status values, JSON/API keys, translation keys, comments, docblocks, test descriptions, internal logs and developer documentation. Preserve established external identifiers and official proper names rather than inventing translations.

Use English semantic keys with translated values, for example results.insufficient_evidence → No hay suficiente evidencia para calcular un resultado. Spanish baseline copy lives in lang/es/*.php; approved regional catalogs use ca, gl and eu. Browser code consumes the same reviewed dictionary through a public build or safe serialization. Longer questions, summaries and editorial explanations live in reviewed localized content, outside scoring logic.

Configure APP_LOCALE=es and APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE=es. Users may explicitly select an enabled reviewed locale from es, ca, gl and eu. Root HTML language and display formatting follow the selected locale. Keep the Eloquent/code pluralizer in English. English UI is outside the agreed scope, and browser language preferences must not select an unsupported English interface.

The Spanish fallback is a runtime safeguard, not permission to publish unfinished regional interfaces. An enabled locale must have complete approved UI/question translations. Detect missing keys before release; unexpected missing strings receive approved Spanish fallback copy with a language indication, never a raw key or English message. Notify operators through internal English diagnostics without recording political answers.

Translate framework and package validation, pagination, authentication and error screens as well as custom UI. Never present an exception message, stack trace, raw status, translation key or machine reason code directly to users. HTTP/API payloads use English stable codes; localized presentation adapters supply visible meaning.

The reference matching module is developer-facing and includes English diagnostic reason strings. When integrating it into the website, expose stable English reason codes and map them to reviewed localized catalogs; do not render current strings directly. Changing language must preserve answers by stable question ID, all weights, scoring, evidence coverage and comparison gates.

Keep programme quotations exact. Translations are separately reviewed, explicitly labelled fields, with the original accessible and its source language marked. Official party/person names and original excerpts retain their original language. Do not silently rewrite source material or treat translated wording as a verbatim quotation. User-facing summaries and explanations follow the chosen approved interface language.

AI may draft translations of public UI copy and programme material. A fluent reviewer must approve each target language, with particular care for Basque and politically or legally nuanced wording. Check against the original and preserve conditions, exceptions, negation, quantified commitments and modal strength. Do not send private questionnaire answers/results to translators or AI services.

Maintain a shared glossary for policy terms, answer scales, unknown evidence and methodological explanations. A question keeps one stable ID and one published scoring rubric across languages. A translation that changes the proposition must be corrected; semantic question changes require editorial review and a versioned release, never a hidden locale-specific scoring change.

CI language gate 1: use template/AST-aware checks for raw visible text and user-facing attributes outside approved content/catalogs. Maintain a reviewed allowlist for proper names and source excerpts. English developer diagnostics and symbolic enum values are permitted; do not use a blanket regex banning string literals.

CI language gate 2: collect static translation-key references and require nonempty reviewed entries for every enabled locale. Dynamic keys require explicit enumerated mappings. Validate placeholders/plural variants and detect duplicate or unresolved keys; exercise error paths. Regional locale activation also requires reviewed question/content coverage. Do not require an English UI catalog.

CI language gate 3: browser checks verify HTML language and representative reviewed copy for questionnaire, results, comparisons, source details, privacy, admin, errors, empty states and exports in every enabled locale. Include keyboard/screen-reader text and formatting. The same synthetic answer IDs must yield identical scores across languages. Keep political inputs out of requests, URLs, logs and analytics.

English code review is mandatory. Naming/casing lint and known disallowed identifiers assist but cannot prove a natural language. Review user copy separately for fluency, neutral wording, comprehension and consistency. Spanish is the launch baseline; activate regional interfaces only as fluent review is complete, with no automatic approval based on machine translation.

Persistent instructions live in root AGENTS.md and an alwaysApply rule at .cursor/rules/project-language.mdc. Transfer them into the future application repository. They are active in this workspace; production lint/CI/browser language checks and actual translations are specified backlog work because only a local Laravel bootstrap exists.

sections.title: 18. Delivery dependencies and capacity
sections.lead: Measure nationwide editorial work before committing to scoring. The cited source explorer has its own release path; questionnaire, regional-language and metrics activation add separate gates.
items: The local foundation is partially complete; remaining production tasks and all adaptive tasks are planned. Owner names, hours and effort estimates remain unassigned; this table records proposed roles rather than completed staffing.

Review capacity formula: unique question/programme-scope assessments × two independent reviews × measured minutes per review / 60, plus acquisition/OCR, adjudication, question pilot, correction and translation hours. Compare this demand with each confirmed reviewer’s available hours and reserve a proposed 20% contingency.

Count reusable programme scopes rather than multiplying every province’s identical ballot entry by every question. National text and local annex differences still require explicit applicability records and their own reviewed evidence where they alter a position.

The pilot must include national, regional and coalition scope plus silence, conditions, conflicting passages and translated sources. Historical documents can exercise extraction in a labelled sandbox; they never count as current-election scoring evidence.

Source-explorer path: scope/inventory → archived verified sources → review workflow → comparison UI → atomic release → enabled-capability checks → beta. Questionnaire path additionally needs the balanced reviewed question matrix, calibrated policy and local matching integration. Conditional feature dependencies are explicit in the task records.

Regional activation and optional metrics are separate branches. They cannot delay a passed Spanish core or relax its privacy/evidence standards. TASK-15 is especially conditional, with no deployment or anonymous-collection promise.

An explorer-only release may have questionnaire disabled and no released question bank. Its manifest marks that capability unavailable; questionnaire-specific version fields and checks are not applicable rather than silently satisfied. Later activation needs its own full acceptance record.

Growing the bank from the earlier roughly 30-question proposal to a 60–100 target increases editorial/review demand. Measure actual throughput first; bank size and adaptive launch are not promised for the calendar target.

sections.title: 19. Requirements and acceptance evidence
sections.lead: Every applicable requirement needs a named accountable owner and recorded proof before publication. Existing synthetic arithmetic evidence satisfies only part of the scoring requirement.
items: Current status: the reference arithmetic was checked on synthetic fixtures. Every real-data, language, production integration, security/privacy, rights, cost and operational gate remains pending. No row is an independent certification.

Evidence records include requirement ID, applicable release/feature/locale, actual owner, verification date, method/report, failures and remediation. A planning document, a passing linter or a reviewer-ID count alone cannot establish source truth, anonymity or impartiality.

Adopt WCAG 2.2 AA as the proposed core accessibility target and verify it with manual checks alongside automation. Accessible local excerpts mitigate inaccessible external originals; do not claim control over third-party party websites.
All-party registry completeness is a different gate from programme availability, question coverage and comparable shared evidence. Report each separately; never silently turn one into another.

The canonical machine-readable plan is electoral-app-development-plan.json. Requirements, tasks, risks and decisions are linked by stable English IDs; the planning renderer validates references and the task dependency graph before generating this document.

Applicability is recorded per capability and locale. REQ-03/04/05 scoring gates apply when the questionnaire is enabled. REQ-07 applies to optional metrics activation; regional content/score checks apply to published regional surfaces. Disabled features are visibly unavailable, never represented as passed.

sections.title: 20. Release integrity, operations and fallback
sections.lead: Publish a coherent version, verify failure paths, and demonstrate recovery before promising campaign-period availability.
items: Release state sequence: draft → reviewed → validated → staged → active; old releases become superseded or withdrawn. Only an approved active manifest points visitors to a release. Publication requires independent editorial approval, compatible schema and successful acceptance checks.

Manifest fields: release ID/time/status, source commit, dependency lockfiles/build provenance, schema/questionnaire/rubric/algorithm versions, pinned comparison policy, registry version, enabled locales, browser/public asset hashes, evidence-bundle hash and editorial approval record. Hashes verify byte integrity; they do not themselves prove editorial truth or trustworthy delivery.

The manifest declares enabled capabilities (source explorer, questionnaire, locales and any approved metrics). Explorer-only releases explicitly disable questionnaire and mark its version fields not applicable. Enabling a capability requires compatible assets and additional acceptance proofs; no feature turns on just because its code exists.

Build from a clean locked environment. Generate immutable content-addressed code/data assets, validate every referenced position/quotation/translation, test the exact staged artefacts and activate the manifest atomically. A partially uploaded bundle or stale mixed cache must fail with localized safe copy, never partial political results.

Pin one release when a questionnaire starts. New source/code releases do not silently alter that in-memory session; offer an explicit restart or refresh with a notice. Local exports record compatible versions and explain that political content leaves the device only through the user’s deliberate export.

Correct a disputed source with a documented, versioned change. Mark or withdraw affected mappings immediately when the evidence cannot support them. Roll back to a compatible verified release, or disable scoring if the earlier release shares the defect. Preserve accessible history with withdrawn status rather than erasing it.

Already downloaded/offline packages cannot be retroactively recalled. They show their source version and last-known status; an online check may offer a corrected public package without submitting answers. Do not promise that an offline old result always knows about later withdrawal.

Proposed performance/recovery targets in section 13 require a named traffic/device profile and recorded load/restore drill before acceptance. Snapshot backup consistency, verify hashes and access permissions after restoration, and document who can publish or roll back.

Monitor uptime, source/extraction failures, review backlog, release integrity, storage/cost thresholds and ordinary server health. Monitoring must exclude answer payloads and affinity results. Publish actual supported correction/on-call hours and ownership before launch.

Fallback order: verified local questionnaire after initial load; validated static public release/source explorer and offline package when the backend is unavailable; cited comparison without broad ranking when evidence is insufficient; Spanish baseline when a regional locale is unready; no optional metrics when its pipeline or budget fails. Test each advertised fallback.

Set budget alerts against the chosen funded ceiling and pause nonessential extraction/AI/metrics jobs at agreed thresholds. Verify provider quota/overage behaviour; do not advertise free hosting or a hard spend cap without evidence. Public user access stays free.

Any later public aggregate feedback publication is a separate feature decision with actual-flow/legal/statistical review. The default private dashboard does not waive collection or publication requirements.

sections.lead: These risks are open planning dependencies, with unquantified likelihood. Baseline decisions are recorded; unresolved decisions block their dependent feature or publication.

Most consequential unresolved dependencies are named independent reviewer capacity, actual common evidence coverage, accountable ownership/rights, funded operations and production privacy/recovery verification.
This review strengthens the plan and checks consistency. It does not collect the real programme corpus, recruit reviewers, obtain legal advice, buy hosting, implement CI or deploy the website.

sections.title: 23. Autonomous engineer protocol
sections.lead: Run eligible tasks continuously within the approved blueprint, stop only dependent work at strict gates, and keep evidence honest.
items: Read AGENTS.md, the canonical plan, project-language-policy.html and plan section 17.
Read applicable Boost skills and version-specific documentation; keep public/synthetic inputs.
Inspect current working tree and the last task journal; preserve user changes.
Select the smallest eligible work item whose prerequisites and applicable human gates have passed.
Implement its stated deliverables only; record any necessary design change before broadening scope.
Run the acceptance-specific meaningful tests and required formatting/build checks; distinguish automated checks from human approval.
Record artifact paths/hashes, command outcomes, limitations and the task status in the journal. Never retain political vectors, secrets or raw private payloads.
Continue with another eligible task without asking for routine reversible implementation choices.

Complete means the specified acceptance evidence exists and passes. A draft, synthetic fixture, date or model assertion cannot replace actual-flow or independent human proof. Completed gated work includes completionApprovalBindings to actual retained human approval packet records; completed unconditional prerequisites are required.

Only explicit human approval for the identified packet hash, capability, locale and action passes a strict gate. The engineer prepares the concrete packet; it cannot approve on the user's behalf or impersonate independent reviewers.

Change to an approved design, evidence set, reviewer independence, release candidate, enabled locale/capability or processor flow reopens the affected gate. Status/journal-only progress does not change the design fingerprint.

After at most three focused attempts at the same failing implementation check, record the failure and a concrete next action, then continue independent eligible work. Never weaken tests or skip requirements to close a task.
Waiting for programmes or human reviewers blocks affected evidence/scoring items only. Use clearly labelled synthetic fixtures for pipeline/UI engineering, never as public current-election evidence.

Stop dependent work at a pending gate or missing human-only input. Continue independent eligible items, then report the consolidated approval/input packet. If all applicable work is complete, provide the final evidence record.

Prepare local code, tests, docs and review packets autonomously within the approved blueprint. No domain purchase, paid provision, external source publication, outbound messages or public deployment without the matching explicit action authorization.
This document does not start a goal, unattended scheduler or recurring automation. A later explicit loop/run instruction uses this protocol and its gates.

No answers, priorities, constituency or affinity in requests, URLs, storage, logs, analytics or Boost. Default questionnaire state stays in browser memory. User-triggered local export must be explicit and separately reviewed.
A ready Spanish cited explorer is independently releasable. Questionnaire, ca/gl/eu and metrics have additional scoped gates; deferred optional work must remain visibly disabled, not marked complete.

GATE-01 is the next review. Approving it starts reversible implementation, with GATE-02–GATE-08 retained for later methodology, actual-flow, external/public action and feature activation.

For each new gate record: authority, timestamp, exact user approval reference, packet hash, approved action, capability, locale and subject version. Never create this record from silence, elapsed time or an agent conclusion.
A repeated gate is evaluated independently per actual capability/locale/action. One acceptance never certifies a broader flow.

Execution-v0.6.0 records explicit finish before reveal and complete post-finish citation/insight requirements. Earlier execution-v0.5.0 approval material is superseded; no implementation/CI/skill install is implied by the design clarification.

sections.title: 27. Progressive and adaptive questionnaire
sections.lead: Ten questions lead to a neutral checkpoint; the user explicitly finishes to reveal cited overlaps or continues without seeing party affinities.
rows: 10 balanced questions → neutral checkpoint → explicit finish/reveal or +5
No party/result spoilers before finish; leaving without reveal remains possible
Evidence/capacity first; no guessed or duplicate issue weight
Unnamed highest comparable overlap at checkpoints; individual party indices only after finish
Common-evidence/short-mode gates apply; no membership probability or sum-to-100 shares
Same-target deterministic bounds and explicit ties
Missing programmes and ambiguous commitments cannot be solved by more answers
Topic coverage, then greatest unresolved pair-gap reduction
No preferred-party/popularity/acceptance objective; all candidacies remain visible
New method version/GATE-02; v1 reference remains unchanged
All branch/order/progress calculations in browser memory
Same complete public bundle; no response-dependent question requests/telemetry
Method, short-mode, privacy and locale gates
Planning specification only; no new app functionality
items: Ten answers can produce useful cited overlaps and explicit limitations. They do not automatically pass broad ordering; the v1 20-answer/15-common-question proposal is not silently lowered. A distinct short-mode policy requires GATE-02 calibration.

Stopping/bounds must refer to the same fixed weights, questions, cohort and scoring target as the published adaptive method. No fixed-bank guarantee may be attached to v1's changing answered-only weights.
Do not promise eventual 100% certainty or keep asking solely to fill a progress bar. 100% response coverage only means this scoped bank is answered.

GATE-02 approves the actual bank, weights, thresholds, ordering, short-mode rules and honest readiness language. GATE-03/GATE-06 must then pass for shipped adaptive flows; fluent regional packs add their scoped gate.

Explicit finish is a local display action, not metrics/transmission/publication consent. Post-finish insights include answered-question agreement/disagreement, weights, exact contextual programme citations, unknowns and access to all candidacies/unanswered public topics without guessed personal overlap.

Retain the user's desired percentage at checkpoints only as an unnamed highest documented overlap, under the reviewed common-evidence/short-mode policy. Coverage/stability stay separate. An insufficient or incomparable evidence set cannot support that headline.

sections.title: 28. Modern, inclusive and trustworthy experience
sections.lead: A contemporary civic interface earns trust through understandable evidence and reliable behaviour across ages, abilities, digital confidence, phones and connections. Exact art direction remains a reviewed prototype decision.
rows: Strong legible typography, generous spacing, restrained civic accents, contrast-tested light/dark themes and equivalent treatment of candidacies.

policy.completionRule: Complete means the specified acceptance evidence exists and passes. A draft, synthetic fixture, date or model assertion cannot replace actual-flow or independent human proof.
