questionnaireDesign.userInstruction: All of this is plan mode; this amendment changes design/specification/backlog only.

flow.initialSelection: Release-pinned ten clear policy questions balanced over 8–10 reviewed domains. Broad means accessible concrete policy, not an inferred left/right identity.
flow.continuation: After ten presented questions, show actual valid-answer count and an unnamed highest-overlap index only if the reviewed common-evidence/short-mode policy permits it, with separate coverage/stability limits. Otherwise show honest insufficient-evidence information. Offer explicit finish-and-reveal or +5, with early finish/exit available. Never identify a matching party, map scores to parties or reveal detailed personalised citations before finish.
flow.genericToSpecific: Prefer reviewed broad questions before niche detail, but revisit uncovered important domains and only ask useful refinements. Genericity never overrides evidence, topic budgets or neutral wording.
flow.shortMode: Ten responses may support a highest-overlap checkpoint index without party identity only under an approved comparable-evidence/short-mode policy; otherwise show coverage/limitations. Explicit finish permits cited provisional details without bypassing broad-ordering gates. Existing v1 20-answer/15-common-question thresholds are not silently lowered.
flow.skipRule: Unsure/skip has no numeric stance, does not count as resolved information, is not guessed and is not repeatedly asked. Presented count and scored-answer count differ.

display.overlapIndex: An index out of 100 for documented policy overlap on the disclosed common answered set; not probability of party membership or voting intention.
display.responseCoverage: 100 × sum of fixed bank weights with actual numeric user answers. Label as coverage of the reviewed scoped bank, not confidence. Excluded domains change the explicitly shown scope.
display.programmeEvidenceCoverage: Show the proportion of the fixed scoped bank with applicable reviewed common evidence and candidacy-specific gaps; missing source evidence is separate from missing user answers.
display.stability: Provisional, unresolved/tied or robust within the exact reviewed bank/cohort/weights. A stronger label needs validated bounds and must name its scope.
forbiddenClaims: 90% sure that you belong to Party X
100% certain which party you should vote for
Skipped beliefs can be inferred from other answers
display.noFabricatedPercent: Do not combine arbitrary factors into a confidence percentage or treat the fraction of simulated completions as a probability. A future calibrated probabilistic claim would require a separately approved model/pilot/privacy design.
display.primaryAfterFinish: When the reviewed shared-evidence comparison permits a leader, headline its weighted overlap index and show close alternatives and limitations. Independent party indices do not sum to 100%; they are not probabilities or literal percentages of accepted promises. More answers may raise or lower them.
display.visibility: Before explicit finish, withhold matching-party identities/logos, party-specific score mappings, ranking and personalised source details. A highest-overlap index without party identity may appear only under the reviewed comparable-evidence/short-mode policy, alongside clearly separate coverage/stability. It is not a confidence probability.

weighting.currentReference: policy-distance-v1.0.0 normalizes priorities over answered domains and base weights within answered topics. Its existing synthetic implementation/verification remains unchanged.
weighting.preferredAdaptiveCandidate: Freeze each active domain budget over the entire release-pinned question bank, then distribute it through reviewed policy-family/question shares. Future answers resolve existing mass rather than creating topic weight. Reuse the similarity formula 1 − |u − p| / 4.
weighting.formula: W(q) = priority(domain(q)) / sum_active_domain_priorities × publishedQuestionShare(q); sum of shares within each domain = 1; sum of active W(q) = 1.
weighting.duplicateRule: Related/duplicated questions share a published policy-family budget; splitting a question cannot increase family/domain influence. A broad question and its detail are not automatically independent evidence.
weighting.methodChange: Fixed-bank weighting is a proposed method change, not silently applied to the v1 score. It requires a new reviewed algorithm version and GATE-02 sensitivity approval before production.
weighting.targetConsistency: Stopping/bounds must refer to the same fixed weights, questions, cohort and scoring target as the published adaptive method. No fixed-bank guarantee may be attached to v1's changing answered-only weights.

bounds.scope: B is the pinned active bank; S is the explicitly selected cohort; C contains questions with applicable reviewed positions for every candidacy in S. Original W is fixed; common weights are W(q)/E, where E = sum_C W(q). E=0 means no common diagnostic.
bounds.unknownUser: For an unanswered/unsure/skipped q use the possible answer set {-2,-1,0,1,2}; for a numeric answer use its singleton. No population priors or guesses.
bounds.partyBounds: For a party i, sum weighted minimum/maximum similarity over those possible user answers on C. These full-common-bank bounds are distinct from v1's answered-question missing-source bounds.
bounds.pairBounds: For a,b in S: d(q,u)=similarity(u,p_aq)−similarity(u,p_bq). G_low(a,b)=100×sum_C(W/E)×min_u d; G_high uses max_u. Both parties use the same hypothetical user answer u for each question.
bounds.boundMeaning: The pair interval contains every completion of the remaining user answers for this fixed common target. It is a deterministic scope-conditional bound, not a statistical confidence interval or whole-manifesto guarantee.
bounds.monotonicity: With unchanged weights/cohort/release and retained numeric answers, resolving an answer can only shrink those fixed-target intervals. Observed overlap may rise or fall; edits, priority changes and changed scope reset diagnostics.
bounds.robustLeader: Only if one candidacy has G_low against every other candidacy greater than the approved near-score margin and all evidence/topic/readiness gates pass may the method state a robust leader for this target.
bounds.ties: Identical or inseparable programme positions can make a unique leader impossible. Show a group/tie; do not invent a winner through lexical order.
bounds.missingEvidence: Unknown/contested party positions remain unknown. Additional answers cannot supply missing manifesto evidence. Restrict mathematics to disclosed common C and withhold broad claims if common coverage/topic thresholds fail.

selector.type: Deterministic, inspectable browser-local uncertainty-reduction heuristic; no machine learning or learned voter-party priors.
selector.eligibility: Unasked reviewed questions from the pinned bank, appropriate tier and policy-family budget, with applicable common evidence for the fixed comparison target. Unsure/skip is not silently revisited.
selector.coverageFirst: Apply released minimum domain coverage and repetition/burden caps before discrimination; do not spend all refinement questions on one high-separation issue.
selector.possibleLeaders: Use conservative pair bounds against every candidacy to identify plausible leaders. A current low observed index is not sufficient to exclude a candidacy from refinement consideration.
selector.candidateVisibility: Any internal priority pruning must have a disclosed bound certificate. All candidacies remain displayed/scored on the same common set; do not delete parties or shrink C to improve a result.
selector.gain: For each eligible q, calculate how much its unanswered pair-gap range contributes for each unresolved plausible pair. Gain(q)=max_pair[100×(W(q)/E)×(max_u d(q,u)−min_u d(q,u))]. Identical stances give zero discriminating gain.
selector.priority: Within coverage/tier constraints, maximize gain divided by a published positive locale-independent response-burden cost; W already includes user domain priority. Tie-break by a published party-independent question key. Translations never change selector weights/costs.
selector.neutrality: No party popularity, poll strength, name/logo/ideology label, target winner, acceptance metric or inferred user demographic enters priority. Rename/reorder parties and negate all axes without changing the chosen semantic question.
selector.noAnswerGuess: Evaluate all five allowable numeric possibilities rather than predicting the person's next belief. 'Expected gain' terminology is reserved for an approved predictive model; this baseline is structural worst-case range reduction conditional on a real answer.
selector.publicExplanation: Explain the next topic plainly as unresolved coverage or a documented distinction; avoid a preferred-party cue in question wording.
selector.fallback: If bounds/model/scope validation fails, show safe provisional overlaps and use a pinned balanced order. Never fabricate readiness. CPU limits get a disclosed fixed-order fallback with identical privacy.

recommendedReasons: A scoped leading group is robust under the approved same-target policy
Remaining reviewed questions add too little discrimination
Programme evidence prevents a stronger comparison
stopping.noForcedHundred: Do not promise eventual 100% certainty or keep asking solely to fill a progress bar. 100% response coverage only means this scoped bank is answered.
stopping.continueWhenStable: Offer party-neutral information about whether another block can help before finish. Users may finish explicitly, then browse sources or knowingly refine for fuller explanations; no automatic reveal.
stopping.allSkipped: Show unavailable/insufficient personal comparison, cited programme browsing and an option to revise responses; never assign a default neutral profile.
stopping.allTopicsExcluded: If all topic priorities are zero or no valid active question/evidence target exists, return unavailable coverage/diagnostics rather than divide by zero or report 100%. Offer scope/priority revision and source browsing.

privacy.bankDelivery: Load the same complete public bank, dictionary and relevant evidence release regardless of responses. No per-next-question request, server-selected branch or response-dependent chunk.
privacy.derivedData: Question order, next-question ID, candidate subset, stop reason, uncertainty ranges and progress are derived political data; keep them in browser memory alongside answers/priorities/constituency. The finish/reveal/refinement flag is local private session state and is not logged or sent.
privacy.telemetry: No adaptive-path, progress, abandonment, timing or result events by default. Optional metrics stay behind their separate actual-flow/aggregation gate.
privacy.localExport: Only an explicit local export may include answers, priorities, order and all algorithm/selector/readiness/bank versions, with a Spanish privacy explanation. Before finish, an explicit answer export must exclude unrevealed party affinities, rankings and personalised citation selections; downloads never serve as an implicit reveal.
privacy.releasePin: Pin bank, scores, selector, readiness, weights, locale dictionaries and evidence together. Locale changes preserve semantic IDs/order/diagnostics; withdrawn source versions invalidate affected conclusions.

proposedChecks: Fixed-target bounds contain all enumerated tiny-fixture completions; pair comparisons use the same hypothetical answer
Party order/labels, question order, axis inversion and duplicated issue splitting cannot manipulate priority/budgets
Neutral vs skip; edited answer, changed priorities/cohort, all-skipped, tied parties and insufficient common evidence
Anchor versus adaptive paths over synthetic profiles at 10/15/20+ questions; convergence is not treated as calibrated probability
Independent human question-order, party-priming, wording/translation and coverage review
Actual no-network/storage/log proof includes derived question IDs/path/stop codes; mobile burden/latency measured

Only a policy-permitted unnamed checkpoint overlap may appear before finish, never party identity, party-specific score mappings or detailed citations across visual/DOM/a11y/notification/title/export/history; check comparable arithmetic, insufficient evidence and intentional post-finish insight parity.
validation.pilotPrivacy: No retained real answer vectors, party identities, voting intentions or learned ideology labels. Use public/synthetic simulations and consented comprehension review under the existing pilot/privacy gate. Distinguish a first pass with hidden affinities from voluntary refinement after seeing results; no political answers are retained.
validation.gate: GATE-02 approves the actual bank, weights, thresholds, ordering, short-mode rules and honest readiness language. GATE-03/GATE-06 must then pass for shipped adaptive flows; fluent regional packs add their scoped gate.

sources.title: A perfect match? The impact of statement selection on voting advice applications' ability to match voters and parties
sources.use: Primary study by Lefevere and Walgrave (2014), reviewed through the university repository abstract, reports that statement selection changes voter-party matching. It motivates independent question-selection/weight review; it does not validate this adaptive method.

sources.title: A New Stopping Rule for Computerized Adaptive Testing
sources.use: Primary simulation study motivates stopping when further items offer little improvement. Its calibrated medical/psychometric model and numeric thresholds are not transferable confidence evidence for political overlap.

resultReveal.finishAction: Only an intentional finish/view-results activation enters finished_revealed. Completing question 10, another block, the final bank item, a timeout or a readiness calculation never triggers it.
resultReveal.beforeFinish: Neutral question/help text and actual presented/valid counts. At checkpoints, optionally show the unnamed highest comparable overlap and a non-identifying close-group/limitation explanation when the reviewed policy allows it. No names/logos, party-specific colours or score mappings, ranking, result preview or personalised programme excerpts; never manufacture a strongest score on incomparable evidence.
resultReveal.afterFinish: A scoped overlap comparison with topic-specific agreement/disagreement, understandable weighting and coverage/stability/missing-source limits. All candidacies remain represented; broad ordering is withheld when its evidence gates fail.
resultReveal.finishIsNotConsent: Finish is a browser-local display choice, never consent to metrics, transmission, storage, sharing or publication. No finish/exit/reveal event is sent by default.
resultReveal.exit: Users may leave without revealing or choose finish at an early point. Zero valid answers, excluded domains or insufficient evidence produce an honest unavailable/limited result, never an invented leader.
resultReveal.refinement: After viewing results, users may explicitly refine. Updated affinities are withheld until another finish activation; retain the pinned release and valid semantic IDs. Previously seen information cannot be unlearned, so informed refinement is distinguished from first-pass neutral evaluation.
resultReveal.publicExplorer: The independent programme comparison remains available without finishing or taking the quiz. It does not automatically display personalised affinities; the complete public evidence bank remains inspectable for open-source verification.
resultReveal.uiBoundary: Withhold matching-party identities, party-specific mappings/rankings and detailed personalised results from visual/hidden DOM, live regions, tooltips, notifications, titles, previews and downloads before finish; do not merely hide a result list with CSS. The explicitly permitted unnamed checkpoint index may render without identity. This controls presentation, not secrecy of public evidence/local calculation.
resultReveal.sourceAccess: After finish, show relevant exact citations for scored answered questions, including disagreement and conditions. Unknown/ambiguous/pending mappings are marked unscored, with reviewed available source information rather than a fabricated justification.
resultReveal.furtherInformation: Provide all-candidacy and topic exploration, full reviewed programme/source links, original excerpts plus labelled translations, scope/date/version, glossary, method/weighting, corrections and optional local reset/export. Unanswered topics are public information only, not inferred personal preferences.

resultReveal.copyStatus: Draft content values awaiting fluent/editorial, comprehension and actual-flow review; identifiers remain English.
resultReveal.futureCi: With synthetic fixtures, whitelist only the permitted unnamed checkpoint index and verify its shared-evidence arithmetic/limitations; assert no matching-party identity, score-to-party mapping or detailed result in visual/DOM/accessibility/title/notification/export surfaces before finish. Cover checkpoints, bank exhaustion, errors, locale/theme and history. Then verify intentional reveal, refinement/re-finish, source parity and no transport/storage/log events. Raw common public data may contain party names.

postFinishInsights.headline: Highest comparable weighted overlap, or an explicit close group/tie/limited evidence state; candidacies on different evidence sets are not mixed into a ranking.
answeredQuestionDetail: User's chosen answer and question meaning
Exact programme excerpt with surrounding conditions, page/locator, source scope/date/version and original link
Unknown/conflicting/pending evidence clearly distinguished and unscored
postFinishInsights.topicInsight: Explain documented overlaps and disagreements across answered topics; avoid cherry-picking only positive matches or labelling the user's identity.
postFinishInsights.additionalExploration: Every relevant candidacy and available reviewed topic remains accessible, including complete programme/source references and methodology/coverage/corrections. Unanswered questions never receive guessed personal overlap.
postFinishInsights.privacy: All personalised expansion/filtering stays browser-local against the same pinned public bundle. Original-source visits and explicit local exports follow their existing honest destination/rights/privacy review; no new remote personalised API or analytics.

experienceDesign.scope: Every enabled public, questionnaire, editorial/admin, help, error, accessibility and export surface; each enabled locale.
experienceDesign.intent: Contemporary civic design that feels welcoming, engaging and dependable across ages, abilities, digital confidence, devices and connections. Universal usability or trust is an aim, never an untested guarantee.

visualDirection.identity: Distinctive civic identity for Nos Vemos en las Urnas, strong readable typography, generous spacing, clear hierarchy, restrained accent colour and tactile controls. Exact palette and typeface remain prototype decisions.
visualDirection.presentation: Responsive editorial layouts and focused questionnaire screens; rich comparison through meaningful interaction and progressive disclosure.
visualDirection.themes: Contrast-tested light and dark token sets, OS preference plus explicit choice; identical evidence, scores and controls in both.
visualDirection.typography: Proposed 18 CSS px body/question baseline, at least 16 CSS px essential secondary copy, comfortable line height and approximately 45–75 characters per reading line; responsive rem-based type and user zoom.
visualDirection.neutrality: The site's main palette and hierarchy must not favour a party. Official party identities, if used with rights, receive equal prominence; colour never encodes truth, affinity or missing evidence alone.
visualDirection.tone: Plain, welcoming, respectful Spanish, with an energetic civic brand. Humour must pass mixed-age comprehension review; policy wording, citations and result limitations remain precise.
visualDirection.assets: Small self-hosted assets with system-font fallback. No third-party font, media, social or tracking embed; optional decorative assets are never required for core use.

journeys.landing: Two clear routes: questionnaire and programme comparison. Explain purpose, current source readiness and practical privacy boundaries before starting; no login or payment.
journeys.questionnaire: One clearly labelled policy question at a time, large answer controls, distinct unsure and skip, back/edit/help and explicit Next. Selection feedback is immediate but does not silently advance. Screen-reader focus and announcements are deliberate and tested.
journeys.checkpoint: After 10 presented questions and each optional +5 block, show actual valid-answer count and, where reviewed common-evidence policy allows, the highest overlap without identifying a party. Label coverage/stability separately. Offer explicit finish/reveal, review, +5 or exit; detailed party results/citations stay hidden.
journeys.results: Only explicit finish reveals the personalised comparison. A concise overlap explanation expands into answered-topic agreement/disagreement, weights, conditions, exact source locators and uncertainty. All candidacies remain accessible with status and a text/table alternative; no broad ranking on unequal or inadequate evidence.
journeys.comparison: Choose public topics/candidacies locally, reveal differences and common commitments, inspect exact original citations and reviewed summaries. Responsive stacked alternatives accompany wide tables.
journeys.source: Source detail is one clear action away from a claim. Expandable evidence retains context, document date/version/page and any conditions. Original quotations remain exact. External source opening is deliberate, with honest destination/access information.
journeys.supportAndAdmin: Help, privacy, corrections, admin, error/empty states and exports use the same legible components, reviewed language and recovery conventions.

interactionAndMotion.motion: Proposed 120–200 ms subtle transitions that explain state change; controls respond before decoration completes.
interactionAndMotion.reducedMotion: Respect prefers-reduced-motion and provide an accessible motion control. Remove nonessential movement while preserving every function, meaning and focus transition. This adopts an additional motion-safety requirement beyond the AA baseline.
interactionAndMotion.progress: Show actual presented/valid counts and optional-block progress. An unnamed highest-overlap index is permitted at checkpoints only under the reviewed comparison policy; it is not completion or confidence. Party identities and their individual score mappings appear only after explicit finish.
interactionAndMotion.control: No forced timing, hover-only information, gesture-only action, drag-only priority setting, custom cursor, scroll hijacking or autoplay. All user actions have keyboard and touch equivalents.
interactionAndMotion.feedback: Use explicit labels and icons/text, visible selection, stable layouts and brief accessible status messages. No celebration of a particular party, fabricated loading delay or vote recommendation.
interactionAndMotion.stop: Exit without results and explicit finish-and-reveal are distinct clear actions. Neither submits or persists political inputs. Explain ephemeral browser-memory state and offer only an explicitly requested, reviewed local export.

accessibility.target: WCAG 2.2 AA for the complete enabled page/process scope, including admin and exports where applicable. No conformance claim until a qualified review documents the actual release and outstanding issues.
accessibility.contrast: Normal text at least 4.5:1; qualifying large text at least 3:1; essential control boundaries/state information at least 3:1 against adjacent colours. Test hover, focus, selected, loading and error states in both themes.
accessibility.targets: Prefer at least 44 by 44 CSS px primary interactive targets, with spacing and a non-overlapping hit area. This is a project design target above the WCAG 2.2 AA minimum.
accessibility.reflow: Core journeys work at 320 CSS px and with 200% text resize/400% zoom, portrait/landscape and user text spacing. Essential wide comparisons have an equivalent operable stacked/text view.
accessibility.semantics: Native controls, labelled groups, headings/landmarks, skip navigation, visible unobscured focus, logical reading order and accessible status/error messages; correct expanded/modal semantics and focus return where overlays are used.
accessibility.alternatives: No meaning relies on colour, motion, sound or a chart alone. Every percentage has a plain-language interpretation; visual comparison has an equivalent text/table presentation.
accessibility.authentication: Editorial authentication must support password managers/paste and accessible recovery; no unaided cognitive puzzle or inaccessible gate.
accessibility.verification: Automated checks supplement manual keyboard, screen-reader, voice-control, touch, zoom, contrast, forced-colour and reduced-motion reviews. Include VoiceOver/Safari and NVDA/Firefox or Chrome, plus mobile assistive technology on named real devices.
accessibility.releaseRule: Unresolved applicable A/AA failures or essential comprehension/access barriers block the affected capability/locale; automated scores alone cannot pass acceptance.

performanceAndReliability.referenceProfile: A named entry-level Android phone with approximately 2 GB RAM plus older iPhone and desktop profiles; an agreed slow-connection profile proposed at 4 Mbps down/150 ms RTT, and a separately documented more constrained connection. Confirm physical device limits and record throttling before treating budgets as committed.
performanceAndReliability.measurement: Measure cold/warm load, full validated-bank readiness, repeated interaction and worst-case selector/bounds on shipped assets with realistic public data and synthetic answers. Record run counts/distributions/device/browser/network/release hashes. Lab thresholds are proposed acceptance budgets, not a claim of field p75 Core Web Vitals.
performanceAndReliability.fieldPrivacy: Core Web Vitals official field thresholds apply at p75 separately for mobile/desktop. No custom RUM, session replay, quiz telemetry or production feedback collection is added to obtain them; non-editorial collection remains default-off under its existing separate gates.
performanceAndReliability.budgetMeaning: The 300 KiB UI budget covers initial HTML/CSS/JS/fonts/essential images; the complete common evidence bank is measured separately within the existing 5 MiB ceiling. That ceiling is not a performance entitlement. Full-bank readiness must also meet the agreed cold-start budget. Preserve every candidacy and citation rather than silently trimming coverage.
performanceAndReliability.loading: Render a useful lightweight Spanish shell/explorer; show truthful cancellable preparation if the full public bank is not ready. Do not allow scoring against partial, unvalidated or mixed releases; no fake progress percentage.
performanceAndReliability.resilience: Validate and pin one release before matching. Once loaded, tested local functions can continue through backend/network outages; original-source access is labelled when unavailable. Public-only caches must exclude answers/results and preserve release integrity.
performanceAndReliability.failureStates: Plan missing/unavailable/withdrawn evidence, bad hashes/schema, slow/failed fetch, interrupted local work, duplicate taps, large source text and correction/rollback. Localized recovery actions never fabricate evidence or transmit state.
performanceAndReliability.degradation: Accessible public browsing/help has a reviewed static/server-rendered path. If questionnaire JavaScript is unavailable, show a Spanish explanation and comparison access rather than submitting answers to a server.
performanceAndReliability.priority: Meaningful content and responsive controls take precedence over decorative media. Remove or simplify an enhancement when it fails accessibility/device/performance/privacy acceptance.

trust.claims: Public confidence comes from verifiable evidence and behaviour: exact citations, visible uncertainty, source coverage/date/version, correction history, methodology, ownership/funding and reproducible code.
trust.privacy: Describe actual browser-memory matching and real hosting metadata honestly; no unsupported anonymous/security/certification badge or promise that source code alone proves neutrality.
trust.agency: Explain policy overlap without labelling a person's identity or prescribing a vote. Encourage participation consistently across parties and respect stop/skip/unsure choices.
trust.presentation: Same visual treatment and evidence standards for each candidacy; unknown is distinct from disagreement. No fake official-election affiliation or party-dependent trust/reward styling.

trust.copyStatus: Illustrative content data only, subject to fluent/editorial and actual-flow review; not an approved public catalog.

humanReview.rounds: At least two formative rounds with revised prototypes/candidate assets, with named design/accessibility owners and capacity agreed before the pilot.
humanReview.coverage: Include young adults approximately 18–30, adults 65+, people with low digital confidence and people using assistive technology. Overlap groups where practical; age never substitutes for ability and no age-based product mode or inference is required.
humanReview.tasks: Use synthetic scenarios to start/skip/edit, stop without reveal, explicitly finish, understand provisional results, recognise absent evidence, find a cited condition/disagreement, compare all parties, knowingly refine/re-finish, reset and recover. Verify no spoilers before finish across ages and assistive technology, for actual proposed capability/locale scope.
humanReview.success: Record concrete barriers, user comprehension and revisions. Essential tasks must be operable; unresolved severe misunderstanding of scores, source status or privacy blocks the affected flow and triggers retesting. A small formative sample cannot certify universal usability or trust.
humanReview.privacy: A separate reviewed participant/consent/retention protocol is required before a human study. Use fictional answer scenarios; no political affiliation, intended vote, real answers, session replay or automatic product metrics. Keep participant contact/recruitment data outside the public repo and separate from deidentified barrier reports; public research artifacts contain no identifiable quotes.
humanReview.authorization: The engineer prepares the protocol and review artifacts. Human recruiting/contact and participant input are supplied or separately authorized by the user; this plan does not authorize outbound messaging.
humanReview.locale: Spanish is complete by default; ca/gl/eu pass the same readability, layout, a11y and comprehension requirements after complete fluent review. Original code and developer documentation remain English.

acceptance.designReview: Review responsive prototypes and state inventories before component rollout; record actual owner decisions and accessibility feedback.
acceptance.productionReview: REQ-09 and REQ-18 evidence on actual candidate assets feeds scoped GATE-03. Questionnaire and regional activation still require GATE-06/GATE-07; optional metrics retain GATE-08.
acceptance.limits: Planning checks and a beautiful prototype do not establish accessibility, performance, trust, neutrality, privacy or production reliability.
